scope: Read all eight complete selected Train texts and the four generated texts' source passages. Selection used maximum wrong-class probability across six completed reports, with separate human collections and model/mixed error directions. These deliberately difficult examples are not representative or unseen evaluation data.

findings: The source is a highly rhetorical narrative summary with long sentences, fantasy, emphatic role names and an extended parenthetical qualification. This register already occurs in Train.
The raw view begins with one ASCII space. The collapsed view removes only that byte; all remaining bytes match. V6 combined model/mixed probability rises from 0.1424530854 to 0.9718453117.
Both base refits assign high combined probability in both views. Their errors are not explained solely by the V6 formatting effect.

The institutional history combines dates, activities and quantitative claims with promotional wording about innovation and leadership. Readability and promotional register do not change its historical-proxy evidence class.
V6 and control assign high combined probability, while consistency keeps both views below one half. This is a selected case of improvement, not evidence of general superiority.

The research abstract uses conventional motivation, methods, findings and implications language, including claims about opportunities and challenges. It contains these patterns within the existing human-proxy Train set.
The two input views are byte-identical. All three detectors assign high combined probability, so this selected failure survives the declared whitespace normalization.
The news report interleaves an incident account, building-security background and victim details. Its source status was not reclassified based on model scores or a new factual audit.

Collapsing paragraph separators lowers control's combined probability from 0.9148404811 to 0.1807473595 and consistency's from 0.6672921743 to 0.1199862171. Whitespace effects therefore occur in either direction across selected sources.

The Qwen direct-profile draft closely follows the source's technical sequence and terminology for errors and residuals. It also adds an explanatory ending and strengthens a qualification about observability.

Recorded draft provenance supplies its model-only label. V6 assigns only 0.0051901764 combined model/mixed probability in either identical view; control and consistency detect model involvement. Technical similarity to the source does not erase generation evidence.
The OLMo source-matched draft closely follows the original character list, suspected espionage and journey. It changes reluctance to refusal and omits or broadens some source details.
All three detectors classify the draft mainly as mixed, but their combined model/mixed probabilities exceed 0.95. This is a three-class provenance error, not a failure to detect model involvement.

The Mistral plain-profile copyedit retains the clustering explanation's progression, technical terms and historical names while rephrasing throughout. The text alone does not disclose that editing operation.

V6 and control assign low combined model/mixed probability; consistency assigns above 0.92 in both views. The record's edit provenance and historical parent support the mixed label independently of those scores.

The OLMo requested copyedit rewrites the narrative extensively and changes several relationships: the dinosaur's first target, who argues afterward and the motive for revenge. It adds self-mockery, guilt and a moral conclusion, and changes reluctant permission to apparent unconcern.

The output does not satisfy the requested light-to-moderate edit. Its process label remains mixed because it is an edit of the human-proxy parent; realized edit intensity and semantic defects need separate annotation.

All three detectors assign combined model/mixed probability above 0.99 while preferring the model-only class. This exposes a distinction between process provenance and visible rewriting intensity. It does not authorize post hoc relabeling.
